fact: The Liberia Telecommunications Authority put its draft Satellite Communications Guidelines (LTA-GLL-002-2026) out for written comment from 23 February to 9 March 2026, asking licensed service providers, satellite operators and other stakeholders for their views, with a public consultation forum scheduled for 5 March.
The LTA states it ran the consultation on the draft Satellite Communications Guidelines in accordance with its published Guidelines for Consultation Process of 2009.

The Liberia Telecommunications Authority held a public consultation on its Draft Infrastructure Regulations at the RLJ Resort in Paynesville with internet service providers, mobile network operators, licensees and other industry stakeholders (consultation date not stated; dated by the 2026-10-12 publication).

The Liberia Telecommunications Authority launched a consultation on its draft Satellite Communications Guidelines on 2026-02-23, inviting written comments, and held public consultation forums with licensed telecom providers on 5 March and 29 May 2026; the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, mobile operators, infrastructure operators, ISPs and satellite companies including Starlink Liberia, Eutelsat OneWeb and Amazon Kuiper took part.

The LTA published a Consultation Report on 2026-04-03 detailing its responses to written stakeholder submissions, and says the final Satellite Communications Guidelines incorporate comments received, for example keeping the five-year NGSO landing-rights term while dropping a seven-day ESIM notice requirement.

The LTA says the consultation on the Satellite Communications Guidelines was conducted under Part III, Section 11(4) of the Telecommunications Act of 2007 and the Consultation Process Guidelines for LTA Rules, Orders and Regulations, 2009.

The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications with the African Union Commission held a two-day multi-stakeholder consultation on 13-14 November 2025 in Monrovia to prepare Liberia's National Data Policy, with representatives of government, civil society, academia, the private sector, development partners and the media.
The Senate joint committee on Post and Telecommunications, Judiciary and Claims and Petition said its review of the draft Cybercrime Act was guided by a public hearing.
